# Geographical and ethnic variation of the 677C>T allele of 5,10 methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR): findings from over 7000 newborns from 16 areas world wide

2003, Journal of Medical Genetics

https://doi.org/10.1136/JMG.40.8.619## AbstractAI


AI

The 677C>T allele of the MTHFR gene is associated with various health conditions, making its geographical and ethnic distribution significant for public health and genetic research. This study analyzes over 7000 newborn samples from 16 regions worldwide, identifying variations in genotype and allele frequency among different populations, which may reflect evolutionary pressures and aid in understanding gene-disease associations. Results indicate notable disparities in distribution, which could inform future investigations into health impacts linked to the MTHFR genotype.

## Key takeawaysAI


AI

- The study analyzes 7130 newborns from 16 global regions to assess the 677C>T MTHFR allele distribution.
- Significant ethnic and geographical variations in the TT genotype frequency were observed, ranging from 4% to 32%.
- Homozygosity of the TT genotype is notably high in Mexico (32%) and southern Italy (26%).
- The research contributes to understanding gene-disease associations and aids in public health genetic assessments.
- Sample collection methods varied by location, ensuring a diverse representation of ethnicities and geographical backgrounds.

## FAQs

AI

## What geographical variations exist for the MTHFR 677C>T allele prevalence?

The study indicates that the homozygous TT genotype peaks at 32% in Mexico, 26% in southern Italy, and 20% in northern China, showcasing marked geographic differences.

## How was the newborn sample population selected across different countries?

Sampling involved systematic methods, such as selecting consecutive newborns from screening programs or hospitals, ensuring comprehensive representation.

## What implications do the findings have for understanding health outcomes related to MTHFR?

The data suggest potential associations between high TT frequency and increased neural tube defects, as seen in Mexico and northern China.

## How do ethnic variations affect MTHFR 677C>T allele distribution?

TT homozygosity is notably high among Hispanic newborns in Atlanta (15%) and Mexican newborns, while low frequencies are found in African ancestry groups.

## What methodological quality controls were implemented to ensure genotype accuracy?

Inter-laboratory consistency was achieved through blind retesting and proficiency testing, resulting in complete agreement across participating laboratories.
